taxonomyNote: NatureServe treats Rallus crepitans as a species; it notes older treatments considered it conspecific with King Rail (AOU 1998), and that Pacific-coast and Colorado River populations have been variously treated as R. longirostris, R. elegans or R. obsoletus (AOU 1983).
fieldMarks: Chicken-sized (35-48 cm) with a long narrow bill and barring on the flanks
Underparts vary from buffy gray on the Atlantic Coast to dull cinnamon on the Gulf Coast
Almost never seen away from salt marsh
behavior: Forages by walking in shallow water or on mud, especially on a falling or low tide, taking prey from the ground or vegetation or probing
Eats mainly crustaceans (crabs, crayfish), also aquatic insects, small fish, mollusks, worms, frogs and sometimes seeds
Found year-round in many parts of its range; some withdrawal from the northern Atlantic end in winter
habitat: Salt marsh, rarely brackish; strictly salt marsh along most of the Atlantic and Gulf coasts, sometimes adjacent brackish marsh, and shallow mangrove swamps in Florida.
range: Coasts of the western Atlantic, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean: Massachusetts south through Florida along the Atlantic, and Florida west to Tamaulipas along the Gulf.
